description: Twenty authored controlled synthetic fixtures. These are not live-web benchmarks or proven unseen held-out questions. Never use expected answers in production prompts.

cases.question: What was the population of Alder in 2025, measured in residents?

sources.title: Controlled fixture numeric-population, document 1
sources.text: Alder population in 2025 was 12,400 residents.

sources.title: Controlled fixture numeric-population, document 2
sources.text: The Alder census used a household register covering the 2025 calendar year; its geographic boundary was the municipal boundary.

sources.title: Controlled fixture numeric-population, document 3
sources.text: The Alder census methodology excluded temporary visitors and counted usual residents only.

cases.question: How much funding did the Beacon program receive in 2025, in USD?

sources.title: Controlled fixture numeric-funding, document 1
sources.text: Beacon received USD 23 million in program funding for fiscal year 2025; this is the awarded total, not an application target.

sources.title: Controlled fixture numeric-funding, document 2
sources.text: Beacon applications were reviewed in three rounds during 2025. Funding awards covered infrastructure and training.

sources.title: Controlled fixture numeric-funding, document 3
sources.text: The Beacon audit separated fiscal year 2025 awards from future pledges; only completed awards were booked.

cases.question: What is the rated operating lifetime of the Cobalt sensor, in hours?

sources.title: Controlled fixture numeric-lifetime, document 1
sources.text: The Cobalt sensor has a rated operating lifetime of 8,600 hours under the standard continuous operating test.

sources.title: Controlled fixture numeric-lifetime, document 2
sources.text: Cobalt lifetime testing used room temperature and nominal voltage. The result concerns operating time rather than storage time.

sources.title: Controlled fixture numeric-lifetime, document 3
sources.text: The Cobalt maintenance note distinguishes its operating lifetime from the separate warranty period.

cases.question: What was the unit purchase cost of the Dahlia pump in EUR during 2025?

sources.title: Controlled fixture numeric-cost, document 1
sources.text: The Dahlia pump unit purchase cost in 2025 was EUR 475 per pump, excluding installation and sales tax.

sources.title: Controlled fixture numeric-cost, document 2
sources.text: Dahlia procurement records separate equipment purchase cost from installation labor. The quoted schedule applies to 2025 orders.

sources.title: Controlled fixture numeric-cost, document 3
sources.text: The Dahlia equipment specification identifies one pump as the procurement unit and excludes accessories.

cases.question: On what exact date was the Elm archive released to the public?

sources.title: Controlled fixture numeric-date, document 1
sources.text: The Elm archive was released to the public on 2025-09-18. This is the public release date rather than the internal approval date.

sources.title: Controlled fixture numeric-date, document 2
sources.text: The Elm archive release included searchable metadata and downloadable records. Internal testing happened before public access.

sources.title: Controlled fixture numeric-date, document 3
sources.text: The Elm archive publication process required a preservation check followed by public release approval.

cases.question: Compare the storage capacity of Iris and Juniper in TB. Report capacity for each system.

sources.title: Controlled fixture comparison-capacity, document 1
sources.text: Iris storage capacity is 24 TB of usable capacity with its standard redundancy configuration enabled.

sources.title: Controlled fixture comparison-capacity, document 2
sources.text: Juniper storage capacity is 36 TB of usable capacity under the same standard redundancy configuration.

sources.title: Controlled fixture comparison-capacity, document 3
sources.text: The Iris and Juniper comparison uses usable rather than raw storage capacity; both systems run the standard configuration.

cases.question: Compare the monthly subscription cost of Kite and Lotus in USD for the standard plan.

sources.title: Controlled fixture comparison-cost, document 1
sources.text: Kite standard plan monthly subscription cost is USD 18 per month, before applicable sales tax and optional add-ons.

sources.title: Controlled fixture comparison-cost, document 2
sources.text: Lotus standard plan monthly subscription cost is USD 27 per month, before applicable sales tax and optional add-ons.

sources.title: Controlled fixture comparison-cost, document 3
sources.text: The Kite and Lotus pricing comparison concerns individual standard plans billed monthly, with no annual commitment.

cases.question: Compare the public availability of Maple and Nori, and their operating lifetimes in hours.

sources.title: Controlled fixture comparison-availability, document 1
sources.text: Maple is publicly available. Maple has an operating lifetime of 900 hours in the continuous-use test at nominal voltage.

sources.title: Controlled fixture comparison-availability, document 2
sources.text: Nori is invitation only. Nori has an operating lifetime of 1,250 hours in the same continuous-use test at nominal voltage.

sources.title: Controlled fixture comparison-availability, document 3
sources.text: The Maple and Nori catalog uses public availability to mean unrestricted ordering. Invitation-only ordering requires prior approval.

cases.question: Compare the 2025 awarded funding for Olive and Poppy in GBP.

sources.title: Controlled fixture comparison-funding, document 1
sources.text: Olive was awarded GBP 6 million in funding in fiscal year 2025. This figure excludes proposed future funding.

sources.title: Controlled fixture comparison-funding, document 2
sources.text: Poppy was awarded GBP 9 million in funding in fiscal year 2025. This figure excludes proposed future funding.

sources.title: Controlled fixture comparison-funding, document 3
sources.text: The Olive and Poppy funding records use the same fiscal year and count awarded funding, not pending applications.

cases.question: Compare Quill and Reed: give each operating lifetime in hours and each unit cost in USD.

sources.title: Controlled fixture comparison-partial, document 1
sources.text: Quill has an operating lifetime of 700 hours and a unit cost of USD 45 per unit under the standard procurement contract.

sources.title: Controlled fixture comparison-partial, document 2
sources.text: Reed has an operating lifetime of 950 hours. The procurement register does not disclose any unit cost for Reed.

sources.title: Controlled fixture comparison-partial, document 3
sources.text: Quill and Reed lifetime tests used identical operating conditions. Reed pricing remains absent from the published register.

cases.question: What population figures do the two records report for Sable in 2025? Identify any same-scope conflict.

sources.title: Controlled fixture conflict-population, document 1
sources.text: Sable municipal population in calendar year 2025 was 41,200 residents, counting usual residents inside the municipal boundary.

sources.title: Controlled fixture conflict-population, document 2
sources.text: Sable municipal population in calendar year 2025 was 44,900 residents, counting usual residents inside the municipal boundary.

sources.title: Controlled fixture conflict-population, document 3
sources.text: The Sable population records use the same municipal boundary, definition of usual residence, and calendar year 2025.

cases.question: What unit cost figures are reported for Tern in the standard 2025 contract? Identify any conflict.

sources.title: Controlled fixture conflict-cost, document 1
sources.text: Tern unit cost under the standard 2025 contract is USD 82 per unit, before tax, for orders of one standard unit.

sources.title: Controlled fixture conflict-cost, document 2
sources.text: Tern unit cost under the standard 2025 contract is USD 96 per unit, before tax, for orders of one standard unit.

sources.title: Controlled fixture conflict-cost, document 3
sources.text: Both Tern price records refer to the same standard 2025 contract and order quantity; neither includes tax or accessories.

cases.question: What rated lifetime figures are reported for Umber in the continuous-use test? Identify any conflict.

sources.title: Controlled fixture conflict-lifetime, document 1
sources.text: Umber rated lifetime is 3,100 hours in the continuous-use test at room temperature and nominal voltage, revision A.

sources.title: Controlled fixture conflict-lifetime, document 2
sources.text: Umber rated lifetime is 3,700 hours in the continuous-use test at room temperature and nominal voltage, revision A.

sources.title: Controlled fixture conflict-lifetime, document 3
sources.text: The Umber records both concern revision A and the same continuous-use test conditions, rather than different hardware revisions.

cases.question: Compare Vale city and metropolitan population figures for 2025. Explain whether scope accounts for the difference.

sources.title: Controlled fixture scope-population, document 1
sources.text: Vale city population in calendar year 2025 was 58,000 residents inside the legal city boundary, excluding surrounding towns.

sources.title: Controlled fixture scope-population, document 2
sources.text: Vale metropolitan population in calendar year 2025 was 132,000 residents across the city and its surrounding commuter towns.

sources.title: Controlled fixture scope-population, document 3
sources.text: The Vale metropolitan boundary contains the legal city and surrounding commuter towns; city and metropolitan totals have different scopes.

cases.question: Compare Willow funding in 2024 and 2025. Explain whether measurement dates account for the difference.

sources.title: Controlled fixture date-funding, document 1
sources.text: Willow awarded funding in fiscal year 2024 totaled USD 12 million. This amount applies only to the fiscal year 2024 awards.

sources.title: Controlled fixture date-funding, document 2
sources.text: Willow awarded funding in fiscal year 2025 totaled USD 17 million. This amount applies only to the fiscal year 2025 awards.

sources.title: Controlled fixture date-funding, document 3
sources.text: The Willow award records use identical program definitions but separate fiscal years. Annual funding may change between years.

cases.question: Compare Xenia equipment-only cost and installed cost in 2025. Explain the cost scope difference.

sources.title: Controlled fixture scope-cost, document 1
sources.text: Xenia equipment-only cost in 2025 is EUR 640 per unit, excluding installation labor and site preparation.

sources.title: Controlled fixture scope-cost, document 2
sources.text: Xenia installed cost in 2025 is EUR 910 per unit, including equipment, installation labor, and site preparation.

sources.title: Controlled fixture scope-cost, document 3
sources.text: The Xenia installed price includes labor and preparation charges that are excluded from the equipment-only price.

cases.question: What was the Fern program budget in 2025, in USD?

sources.title: Controlled fixture unanswerable-budget, document 1
sources.text: Fern operated a training program during fiscal year 2025. The published annual report does not disclose a program budget.

sources.title: Controlled fixture unanswerable-budget, document 2
sources.text: Fern delivered training across several regional centers. The activity register names locations without listing financial amounts.

sources.title: Controlled fixture unanswerable-budget, document 3
sources.text: Fern participant feedback describes course accessibility and teaching quality; the survey contains no financial information.

cases.question: What is the approved 2028 funding for Yarrow in USD?

sources.title: Controlled fixture unanswerable-future, document 1
sources.text: Yarrow is preparing a funding request for fiscal year 2028. No funding amount has been approved or published for that year.

sources.title: Controlled fixture unanswerable-future, document 2
sources.text: Yarrow planning documents describe a future expansion proposal and say that an award decision is pending.

sources.title: Controlled fixture unanswerable-future, document 3
sources.text: Yarrow governance requires a formal approval before proposed funding becomes awarded funding. The latest record reports no approval.

cases.question: Is Zinnia publicly available for unrestricted ordering?

sources.title: Controlled fixture unanswerable-availability, document 1
sources.text: Zinnia is described in an engineering research note. The note contains no statement about ordering or public product availability.

sources.title: Controlled fixture unanswerable-availability, document 2
sources.text: Zinnia testing focused on thermal behavior under nominal load. Procurement and customer access were outside the test scope.

sources.title: Controlled fixture unanswerable-availability, document 3
sources.text: The Zinnia methods appendix documents laboratory calibration and safety procedures, with no distribution or ordering policy.

cases.question: On what exact date was the Acorn dataset first publicly released?

sources.title: Controlled fixture unanswerable-date, document 1
sources.text: Acorn dataset documentation describes a collection of archived measurements. It does not identify the first public release date.

sources.title: Controlled fixture unanswerable-date, document 2
sources.text: Acorn metadata uses version labels and contributor names. No public release timestamp appears in the available metadata.

sources.title: Controlled fixture unanswerable-date, document 3
sources.text: The Acorn preservation note describes file formats and archive checksums but omits the history of public distribution.
